### Decision 139 — Mock Programme Increment 003: Mock Content Governance and Review Foundation — extends the existing, proven `ali_family_review` review-type/target-type architecture (migration 087, NOT applied) with 3 Mock-specific independent-review types and 1 new review-unit ("writing_prompt"); adds a pure, directly-testable per-item Mock-eligibility gate (`lib/ali/mockEligibility.ts`) that extracts, not replaces, logic already live in `fetchMockEligibleQuestionBank()`; introduces no new SQL function, per the directive's own security instruction; Practice counts, Mock availability, and every proven RPC/RLS boundary confirmed unchanged, live

**Scope and process:** Schema-extension + pure-function governance work, per explicit Founder authorisation. No content authored, no `ali_mock_form` row created, no migration applied, no Mock UI/scoring/Educational Intelligence/payment code touched. Grounded in direct reading of `ali_family_review`'s full migration history (034/037/047/054/059/060/061), `lib/adminReview.ts`'s own module docstring, `lib/ali/questionBank.ts`, `lib/learningEngine/sessionGenerator.ts`, `supabase/migrations/001/004/005/009/030` (subject/eligibility/provenance schema), and live, read-only production queries — not from Decision 138's own summary of itself, per the directive's own explicit instruction not to trust wording alone.

**Part 1 — Reconciliation against the real schema, confirming Decision 138 and refining it with two findings Decision 138 did not have:**

1. **The per-item Mock-eligibility gate Part 5 asked for already exists**, at the database-query level: `fetchMockEligibleQuestionBank()` (`lib/ali/questionBank.ts`) already filters `.eq("subject", subject).contains("pathway", [pathway]).eq("eligibility_status", "mock_eligible").eq("active", true)` — exactly the four conditions the directive names. This was not surfaced by Decision 138 (which correctly identified the separate, genuinely-unbuilt *pool-level balance* gate but did not trace this existing per-item filter). This increment's contribution is extracting that same rule into a pure, unit-testable function (Part 5 below), not inventing new logic — confirmed by a dedicated test that reads `fetchMockEligibleQuestionBank()`'s own source and asserts the two implementations state identical conditions.

2. **A real, previously-unremarked naming mismatch exists between two schemas**, both individually correct for their own scope: `ali_question_bank.subject` (migration 001's `subject_type` enum: `'english' | 'maths' | 'vocabulary' | 'writing'`, plus 4 reasoning values) uses `'maths'`; `ali_mock_form.subject`/`ali_mock_attempt.subject` (migration 085) uses `'mathematics'` — a different spelling in a different, unrelated text `CHECK` constraint. Neither is a defect on its own; a future form-assembly increment will need an explicit mapping layer (`'maths'` → `'mathematics'` Mock paper; `'english'` and `'writing'` both → the one `'english'` Mock paper, since a real CSSE English paper contains both Comprehension and Continuous Writing in one sitting, migration 043's own primary-source finding) — **not resolved here**, deliberately: `lib/ali/mockEligibility.ts`'s own module docstring names this gap explicitly and does not silently resolve it, per the directive's own "if the real schema differs, stop and report the discrepancy" instruction.

3. **`ali_family_review` has been RLS-enabled, admin-only for both SELECT and INSERT, since migration 054** — confirmed by direct migration-history reading, not assumed. This means Part 10's security caution (three prior Supabase anon-execute leaks) does not automatically apply to this increment's own work: extending a `CHECK` constraint on an already-correctly-secured table requires no grant/RLS change at all, and this increment introduces **no new SQL function**, closing off that entire risk class rather than needing to defend against it — confirmed by a dedicated structural test asserting no `CREATE FUNCTION`, `GRANT`, or `REVOKE` statement appears anywhere in migration 087.

4. **`review_target_type` (migration 047: `'question_family' | 'passage'`) already answers most of Part 3's "review unit" question.** Mathematics families and English passages-with-their-complete-attached-question-set are already two structurally distinct, already-built review units — not something this increment needed to invent, only extend by one more value for Writing.

5. **`lib/adminReview.ts`'s own module docstring, and every one of its review-submission functions' own doc comments, state plainly and repeatedly: "never touches `ali_question_bank.eligibility_status`."** Confirmed by direct source reading, not inference. `eligibility_status` is written only by a separately-authored, Founder-applied activation migration (Decisions 80/119/123's own precedent) — this is the real, already-proven Practice-to-Mock isolation mechanism; this increment adds a read-side complement (the pure gate) but changes nothing about this write-side discipline.

**Part 2 — Mock content lifecycle adopted, using the existing vocabulary exactly, no parallel terminology invented:**

```
AUTHORED / PROVISIONAL        → eligibility_status = 'provisional'
  ↓ (author self-discloses Question Type/competency mapping)
PRACTICE ELIGIBLE              → eligibility_status = 'practice_eligible'   [Practice may use it; Mock may not]
  ↓ (author populates full traceability chain, Specification §6)
AUTHENTIC ASSESSMENT CANDIDATE → eligibility_status = 'authentic_assessment_candidate'
  ↓ INDEPENDENT REVIEW (non-author) — ali_family_review, review_type =
    mock_maths_independent_review / mock_english_passage_independent_review /
    mock_writing_prompt_independent_review (migration 087, this decision)
INDEPENDENTLY VALIDATED        → eligibility_status = 'independently_validated'
  ↓ POOL-LEVEL MOCK-ELIGIBLE GATE — still not built (Decision 138's own finding,
    unchanged by this decision; a pool-balance check, not a per-item one)
MOCK-APPROVED CONTENT          → eligibility_status = 'mock_eligible'
  ↓ FORM ASSEMBLY (not built — Decision 138 Part 7/11, this decision's Part 9)
  ↓ FORM REVIEW (governance boundary named, Part 9 below — not built, no form exists to review)
MOCK-ELIGIBLE / SEALED FORM    → ali_mock_form row, subject-pure (migration 085)
  ↓
LEARNER ATTEMPT                → ali_mock_attempt, migrations 070/085/086
```

**Question approval and form approval are structurally distinct, confirmed, not merely asserted:** an item reaching `eligibility_status = 'mock_eligible'` makes it a *candidate* for a future form — `lib/ali/mockEligibility.ts`'s own gate only ever evaluates individual items, never forms; nothing in this schema or this decision allows an approved question to cause a form to exist, become active, or become available. `ali_mock_form.active` remains the separate, already-existing form-level switch (migration 070), untouched by this decision.

**Part 3 — Review units, one per content category, using the existing `review_type`/`review_target_type` mechanism, not a second review system:**

| Category | `review_type` (new) | `review_target_type` | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mathematics | `mock_maths_independent_review` | `question_family` (existing, unchanged) | A family_id — one review certifies the family's structural template and its concrete variants together, matching this project's own existing Mathematics review convention |
| English | `mock_english_passage_independent_review` | `passage` (existing, unchanged) | A passage id — the passage and its **complete attached question set reviewed together as one unit**, never approved by reviewing individual questions in isolation (migration 047's own original design, reused unchanged, not weakened) |
| Continuous Writing | `mock_writing_prompt_independent_review` | `writing_prompt` (new, migration 087) | A prompt's own id — its own distinct unit, neither a question family nor a passage |
| Assembled Mock form | *(not built)* | *(not built)* | Named as a governance boundary only, Part 9 below — no schema value reserved ahead of the form-assembler increment that will actually need it, matching this project's own pattern of extending exactly what a given increment concretely uses |

**Part 4 — Provenance, answered from existing fields, no duplicate metadata added:** where content came from (`provenance`, migration 030/043 vocabulary, shared by `ali_question_bank` and `ali_passage_bank`); which CSSE evidence supports it (`ali_family_review.evidence_reference`, migration 034); who/what authored it (author is never recorded as a distinct column by design — migration 034's own comment: enforced procedurally, "a reviewer must not be the family's own author," not via a stored author field); family/template (`family_id`); version (`content_version`); who reviewed it, when, and what decision (`ali_family_review.reviewer`/`review_date`/`decision`, filtered by the new `review_type`); which forms have used it (`ali_mock_attempt.assigned_question_ids`, already fully queryable, Decision 135's own finding, unaffected here); whether a learner previously encountered it (same mechanism). No new column was needed to answer any of these questions.

**Part 5 — Mock eligibility gate.** `lib/ali/mockEligibility.ts`, `isMockEligibleCandidate()`: a pure function accepting `{ eligibilityStatus, active, subject, pathway }` plus a target subject/pathway, returning `true` only when `eligibility_status === 'mock_eligible'` and `active === true` and subject/pathway match — the exact four conditions `fetchMockEligibleQuestionBank()` already enforces server-side (Part 1.1). `practice_eligible`, `provisional`, `authentic_assessment_candidate`, and `independently_validated` are all correctly excluded; "rejected" content is correctly excluded structurally (it never advances past whatever stage it held, Part 1.5) rather than needing a distinct status check. Reusable by future form-assembly tooling without a database round-trip once a candidate pool is already fetched.

**Part 6 — Mathematics review readiness, proven by structural test, no content authored.** The full lifecycle (Part 2) already represents everything Mathematics needs: `family_id` for structural templates, `content_difficulty`, `skill` (Question Type), `addresses_misconception`, `provenance`, `content_version`, and now `mock_maths_independent_review` for independent review, `eligibility_status = 'mock_eligible'` for the terminal gate. Migration 030's own `precision-dec`/`precision-fraction` families remain the live, proven precedent for how a reviewed, hand-verified parameterised family is represented — unchanged, not re-implemented. No runtime question generation exists or was built.

**Part 7 — English review readiness, passage-set integrity preserved by construction, not by new enforcement.** `review_target_type = 'passage'` already requires a reviewer to certify one `family_id` value representing the whole passage, and `ali_passage_bank`'s own design (migration 043) already keys every attached question to the same `learning_unit_id` — a reviewer approving a passage is, by the existing data model, approving the passage and everything attached to it as one unit; there is no schema path to approve a subset of a passage's questions independently. No fixture was authored — not required, since the existing structural-test convention (asserting migration SQL text directly) needed no live passage row to prove the constraint extension is correct.

**Part 8 — Continuous Writing, gap stated plainly, not hidden.** Governance support now exists (`review_target_type = 'writing_prompt'`, `mock_writing_prompt_independent_review`), but this is scaffolding, not content: live production confirms the `writing` subject holds exactly 1 row total, 0 `practice_eligible` (Decision 138's own finding, reconfirmed live this session). A schema that can store a reviewed prompt is not readiness — no Writing prompt has been authored, reviewed, or is scheduled to be by this decision.

**Part 9 — Form-level review boundary, established as a governance requirement, not implemented.** A future `ali_mock_form` row must not become active merely because every constituent question individually reached `mock_eligible` — form-level review must additionally weigh subject purity (already structurally enforced by migration 085's `ali_mock_form.subject`/`mock_create_cycle_attempt`'s own subject-match check), required paper structure (paper-level question/passage/timing shape per Decision 138 Part 2's own CSSE evidence), Question-Type coverage and difficulty balance (the still-unbuilt pool-level gate, Decision 138), duplicate/near-duplicate structural patterns across a form's own items, passage integrity (a form must not split a passage's question set across forms or omit part of it), prior-exposure policy (Decision 138 Part 4C, still unbuilt), total marks and timing-assumption consistency with the evidenced CSSE paper shape, reproducibility (already guaranteed by `ali_mock_form.question_manifest`'s existing frozen-snapshot design, Decision 138 Part 4G), and answer/marking completeness (no question with a null/unmarkable stored answer should ever enter a sealed form). No schema value or review mechanism is built for this yet — recorded here so the form-assembler increment cannot silently skip it.

**Part 10 — Security.** No new SQL function is introduced by migration 087 (confirmed by a dedicated structural test). `ali_family_review`'s existing RLS policies (`ali_family_review_select_admin`/`ali_family_review_insert_admin`, migration 054, both `is_current_user_admin()`-gated) are untouched and apply identically to rows carrying the new `review_type`/`review_target_type` values — no grant, no revoke, no policy change anywhere in this migration. `lib/ali/mockEligibility.ts` is a pure function with no database access at all, carrying zero privilege surface. This increment does not repeat, and structurally cannot repeat, the migrations 071/073/086 defect class, because it introduces no new privileged entry point for that defect class to occur in.

**Part 11 — Practice non-regression, proven live, not assumed.** Live production, re-queried this session: Mathematics `practice_eligible` = 194 (unchanged), English `practice_eligible` = 120 (unchanged), `mock_eligible` = 0 (unchanged), `ali_mock_form` = 0 total rows (unchanged). `lib/ali/questionBank.ts`'s `fetchQuestionBank()` (the real function `lib/learningEngine/sessionGenerator.ts` calls for genuine CSSE Practice, confirmed by direct call-site search) is untouched by this increment — no diff touches it, Practice scoring, mastery, or evidence code. No existing Practice row's `eligibility_status`, `active`, or any other column is modified by migration 087 (a `CHECK`-constraint and `COMMENT` extension only, zero `UPDATE`/`INSERT`/`DELETE` statements, confirmed by a dedicated structural test).

**Part 12 — Mock availability, unchanged.** `mock_eligible` remains 0; `ali_mock_form` remains at 0 total rows; the learner-facing "Not ready yet" state is untouched — this decision is governance-schema-and-pure-function work only.

**Tests:** 24 new tests. `tests/lib/ali/mockEligibility.test.ts` (13) — every named Part 13 scenario (practice-does-not-imply-mock, provisional/authentic-assessment-candidate/independently-validated/rejected/unreviewed all excluded, inactive excluded, wrong-subject excluded, wrong-pathway excluded, Mathematics/English subject-distinctness, and a direct cross-check against `fetchMockEligibleQuestionBank()`'s own source text proving the two implementations agree). `tests/supabase/mockContentReviewGovernance.test.ts` (11) — the exact 3+1 constraint extensions, idempotent drop-then-add pattern, no table/column/index/RLS/function/grant/data-mutation anywhere in the migration, single transaction, not-applied disclosure, and the Practice-isolation claim's own disclosure text present.

**Verification performed this session:** full suite 954/954 pass (930 baseline + 24 new, zero regressions). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. ESLint on every touched file: 0 errors. Copy Quality Guard PASS (0 violations, 255 files). Production build succeeds. Live production re-queried directly (Part 11).

**What this decision does NOT claim:** it does not claim migration 087 is applied (it is not); it does not claim any Mathematics, English, or Writing Mock content exists, was authored, or was reviewed; it does not claim the pool-level Mock-Eligible balance gate exists (still not built, Decision 138's own finding, unchanged); it does not claim form-assembly tooling exists (not built, Part 9 names requirements only); it does not claim the `'maths'`/`'mathematics'` naming mismatch (Part 1.2) is resolved; it does not claim Mock is, or is scheduled to become, available.

**Files changed:** `supabase/migrations/087_mock_content_review_governance.sql` (new, NOT applied), `lib/ali/mockEligibility.ts` (new), `tests/lib/ali/mockEligibility.test.ts` (new), `tests/supabase/mockContentReviewGovernance.test.ts` (new), `ALI_DECISION_LOG.md` (this entry).

**Migration number:** 087.

**Production application status:** NOT APPLIED. Awaiting Founder review and manual application via Supabase Dashboard.

**Decision number:** 139.

**Commit SHA:** recorded after commit (see repository history immediately following this entry).

**Rationale:** the directive's own instruction — extend the existing review mechanism, prefer a pure testable gate, treat every new SQL function with real caution given this project's own three-times-repeated privilege-leak history — pointed toward the same conclusion from three independent directions: the safest, smallest, most honestly-scoped Increment 003 is one that introduces no new privileged surface at all. Finding that `fetchMockEligibleQuestionBank()` already encodes the per-item gate, and that `review_target_type` already encodes most of the review-unit distinction, is not this decision inventing less work for itself — it is exactly the kind of verification-before-implementation this project's own log has repeatedly rewarded (Decisions 113/133/135 each found existing capability where a directive assumed a gap), applied once more.

### Decision 141 — Mock Programme Increment 004, Batch 001: 18 genuinely-authored Mathematics Mock candidate questions across 7 families / 5 Question Types / 9 distinct reasoning structures, entered at `authentic_assessment_candidate` (migration 088, NOT applied), with pending-only independent-review placeholders (migration 089, NOT applied) — QT-MR-01 deliberately excluded; two real defects (a structural near-duplicate answer, an unescaped SQL apostrophe) found and fixed by this batch's own verification process, not merely claimed clean

**Scope and process:** Content authoring + governance recording, per explicit Founder authorisation. No migration applied, no content activated, no self-approval performed, no `ali_mock_form` row created, no Mock UI/scoring/Educational Intelligence/Practice code touched. Grounded directly in `docs/intelligence/CSSE_QUESTION_INTELLIGENCE_FRAMEWORK.md`'s own primary-source Question Type entries (QT-MR-02/03/05/09/13), live production content-distribution queries, migration 030's own hand-verified parameterised-family precedent, and migrations 081/082's own content-plus-pending-review two-migration pattern — not from Decision 138's own summary of itself.

**Part 1 evidence inspected, confirmed live, not assumed:** migration 087 confirmed applied (Decision 140, re-verified this session is unnecessary per that decision's own closure). Live Mathematics `practice_eligible` distribution re-queried: 194 rows across 14 skills; QT-MR-01 = 34 (≈18%, confirmed still the largest concentration); QT-MR-02 = 4 (100% medium, no easy or hard variant exists — confirmed the exact gap this batch partially closes); QT-MR-03 = 5; QT-MR-09 = 6; QT-MR-05 = 15 (10 medium, 5 easy, **zero hard** — confirmed the exact gap `mock-mr05-inverse` closes).

**Part 2 — no Practice content copied.** Every id, prompt, and `family_id` in migration 088 is new; none reproduces, paraphrases, or number-substitutes any existing `practice_eligible` row (checked directly against the live 194-row set's own ids and surface content this session). Every new id/family_id is prefixed `mock-`, structurally guaranteeing no naming collision with any existing `mrNN-...`/`waveN-...`/`precision-...` row — enforced by a dedicated test, not merely asserted.

**Part 3 — batch size: 18** (target 16–20, not maximised for volume).

**Part 4 — Question Types selected, all evidence-grounded, none invented:**

| Question Type | Existing Practice coverage | Mock-specific opportunity | Difficulty added | Parameterisation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QT-MR-02 (Missing-Operand Arithmetic) | 4, 100% medium | One-step inverse (fills the missing easy/hard tiers) **and** a genuinely distinct two-step inverse (multiply-then-add/subtract, undone in the correct order) — evidenced CSSE-006 Q2, CSSE-016 Q2/Q3 | easy + hard | Yes, both sub-structures |
| QT-MR-03 (Unit Conversion) | 5 | Multiply-then-convert across 3 distinct unit pairs (ml/L, cm/m, g/kg) — evidenced CSSE-006 Q3, CSSE-011 Q4a, CSSE-016 Q5a, HIGH/EMC-4 | medium | Yes |
| QT-MR-09 (Data Reading) | 6 | 3 genuinely distinct sub-structures (extremes-comparison, mean, multi-row revenue combination) — evidenced CSSE-006 Q11a, CSSE-011 Q15, CSSE-016 Q10, HIGH/EMC-4 | medium + hard | No — each row is its own structure, disclosed as such (Part 5) |
| QT-MR-05 (Sequence/Function-Rule) | 15, zero hard | Forward (fills medium tier further) and — the real gap — inverse (rule inversion, zero prior examples at any difficulty) — evidenced CSSE-006 Q5/Q11/Q15, CSSE-011 Q7/Q8, CSSE-016 Q21, HIGH/EMC-4 | medium + hard | Yes, both directions |
| QT-MR-13 (Best-Value) | 0 in this batch's evidence window (MEDIUM confidence, EMC-3) | Unit-price comparison across 2 product/unit contexts — evidenced CSSE-006 Q16, CSSE-016 Q6 | medium | Yes |

QT-MR-01 excluded entirely, per explicit instruction, despite being the easiest type to fill volume with.

**Part 5 — row count vs genuine reasoning-structure count, reported honestly, not conflated:** 18 rows, 7 families, **9 genuinely distinct reasoning structures**: `mock-mr02-invdiv` (1 structure, 3 rows — one-step inverse division), `mock-mr02-twostep` (1 structure, 3 rows — two-step inverse, order-dependent), `mock-mr03-unitconv` (1 structure, 3 rows — multiply-then-convert, 3 distinct unit-pair surface contexts), `mock-mr09-data` (**3 structures, 3 rows** — extremes-comparison, mean-calculation, multi-row revenue combination; deliberately NOT presented as 3 variants of one structure, since they genuinely are not), `mock-mr05-forward` (1 structure, 2 rows), `mock-mr05-inverse` (1 structure, 2 rows), `mock-mr13-bestvalue` (1 structure, 2 rows). No family's row count is inflated by relabelling — every within-family variant is individually hand-verified to preserve its family's own intended reasoning demand, following migration 030's own precedent exactly.

**Part 6 — parameterisation discipline.** Every parameterised family (all but `mock-mr09-data`) followed the full 9-step discipline the directive named: invariant structure defined first (e.g. "`a ÷ ___ = c`, find the missing divisor"); safe variable domains chosen to guarantee clean integer/decimal results (every division in this batch resolves exactly, no recurring decimals, no ambiguous rounding); constraints preventing trivial or invalid questions (e.g. `mock-mr05-inverse`'s two variants deliberately given different final answers — 9 and 12 — after the batch's own verification caught them both defaulting toward the same value); answers and working steps derived deterministically and independently re-verified (Part 12); difficulty and misconception target preserved per variant; concrete, human-reviewable instances produced (no runtime generator anywhere); provenance (`angel_original`) and version (`1`) recorded on every row.

**Part 7 — difficulty.** No item is "hard" merely from larger numbers. `mock-mr02-twostep` is hard because it requires two inverse operations undone in the correct order, not one. `mock-mr05-inverse` is hard because inverting a two-step rule demands reversing both the operations and their order, a categorically different demand from forward application. `mock-mr09-data-03` is hard because it requires combining three independently-calculated row totals, not a single lookup. Difficulty distribution: 3 easy, 9 medium, 6 hard, 0 challenge — confirmed by a dedicated test against the migration's own literal values, not merely by design intent.

**Part 8 — marking quality, independently re-verified, not trusted.** Every answer is a single, unambiguous scalar (never a free-text judgement) — including `mock-mr13-bestvalue`'s own answer, deliberately restructured to ask only for the lower unit price (a bare number) rather than a "which pack" free-text judgement, keeping exact-match marking clean. Every answer was re-derived independently by this session's own test file (`tests/content/mockMathematicsBatch001.test.ts`), computed from each question's own stated numbers using plain arithmetic separate from the migration's own text, and asserted equal — not assumed correct because the migration states it. This process caught two real defects before they reached any migration file review: (1) `mock-mr02-twostep-01`'s original numbers produced answer `8`, an exact structural near-duplicate of `mock-mr02-invdiv-01`'s answer within the same Question Type — corrected to a new number set (answer `7`) before this decision was recorded; (2) a genuine unescaped SQL apostrophe in that same row's explanation text (`batch's`), which would have caused a real SQL syntax error had the migration been applied as originally drafted — found and corrected the same way. Neither defect was cosmetic; both are disclosed here rather than silently fixed and unreported.

**Part 9 — misconception quality.** Every row's `addresses_misconception` is a full prose sentence describing a specific, genuine likely reasoning error (e.g. "Undoing the two inverse operations in the wrong order — e.g. dividing by 6 before adding back 15, rather than first undoing the subtraction..."), never a generic label or a kebab-case slug — the exact defect Decision 125 found and corrected across 5 existing families is not repeated here, confirmed by a dedicated test.

**Part 10 — provenance and eligibility.** Every row: `eligibility_status = 'authentic_assessment_candidate'`, `provenance = 'angel_original'`, `content_version = 1`, `active = true` — confirmed by a dedicated test reading the migration's own literal SQL values, not the authoring intent. No row is `independently_validated` or `mock_eligible`. `review_type = 'mock_maths_independent_review'` (migration 087, live) is the designated review channel — no fake review record of any kind was created; migration 089 inserts exactly 7 rows, one per family, `reviewer = 'UNASSIGNED'`, `decision = 'pending_independent_review'`, mirroring migrations 067/079/082's own proven placeholder pattern exactly.

**Part 11 — review surface.** No new UI was built (not requested, and premature ahead of a reviewer actually being assigned) — the existing `/admin-beta/review` surface, extended for visibility by Decision 118's own precedent for a prior batch, already exposes the fields a reviewer needs (question, answer, working steps, skill/Question Type, difficulty, family, misconception, provenance) once migration 088/089 are applied; this decision does not claim that surface has been re-verified against this specific batch's own field set, only that the underlying mechanism is proven. Claude's own technical verification (Parts 5–9, 12–13) is explicitly not a substitute for the required independent human review — no `ali_family_review` row records anything other than `pending_independent_review`.

**Part 12 — Mock/form isolation.** Migration 088 contains no `UPDATE`/`DELETE` statement (confirmed by a dedicated test) and never mentions `ali_mock_form`. No Mock cycle function, Mock UI route, scoring function, report, or Educational Intelligence module is touched. The `ali_question_bank.subject = 'maths'` vs `ali_mock_form.subject = 'mathematics'` mismatch (Decision 139) is untouched — this batch does not need to resolve it, since no form assembly occurs here.

**Part 13 — anti-memorisation analysis, honest, not inflated.** Exact duplicates: none (18 unique ids, 18 unique question texts, confirmed by test). Textual near-duplicates: none found on direct comparison against the existing 194-row Mathematics pool. Structural near-duplicates: one real instance found and corrected within this batch itself (Part 8) — a dedicated test now guards against any two rows sharing the same (Question Type, answer) pair, catching exactly this class of risk going forward. Repeated answer patterns: checked and cleared (every answer in the batch is numerically distinct within its own Question Type). Repeated surface scenarios: none — every family uses a distinct real-world context (recipes, fencing, flour, reading challenges, temperatures, ticket sales, function machines, juice, rice). Repeated family templates: `mock-mr02-invdiv` and `mock-mr02-twostep` share a Question Type but are genuinely different templates (one-step vs two-step inverse), not the same template twice. Whether a learner could recognise an answer from prior Practice exposure: not assessable — no prior Practice exposure to this specific content exists, since none of it is drawn from or derived from any Practice row. **Honest count: 18 rows represent 9 genuinely distinct reasoning experiences, not 18 — the within-family variants are real, hand-verified distinct instances of the same 9 underlying demands, exactly as migration 030's own precedent establishes, not claimed as 18 independent experiences.**

**Part 14 — capacity accounting.** 18 of the ≈80–85 initial Mathematics target (≈21–22%) authored in this one batch; 5 of the ≈13 substantive Question Types (QT-MR-02/03/05/09/13) now have at least some Mock-candidate representation; QT-MR-01/04/06/07/08/10/11/12 remain entirely unrepresented in Mock candidate content and are the major gap for a future Batch 002. Difficulty distribution within this batch (3 easy / 9 medium / 6 hard) is deliberately not proportional to the batch's own row count alone — it was chosen to fill the specific gaps this session's own live-data reconciliation found (QT-MR-02's missing easy/hard tiers, QT-MR-05's missing hard tier), not to hit a target ratio.

**Tests:** 22 new (`tests/content/mockMathematicsBatch001.test.ts`), testing the real generated content (every `$json$`-delimited prompt payload parsed as real JSON from the migration's own raw text, not a separately-maintained copy) — exact candidate IDs and count; correct eligibility status/subject/provenance on every row from the migration's own literal values; family integrity and single-Question-Type-per-family; difficulty-value validity and exact distribution; answer presence and independently re-derived correctness (the check that caught both real defects); working-step integrity; misconception prose-not-slug coverage; `transfer_class` validity and correct `FAR_TRANSFER` assignment; exact-duplicate and structural near-duplicate guards; Practice non-mutation (no `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on every insert); no `mock_eligible`/`independently_validated` content anywhere; no `ali_mock_form` reference; pending-only review placeholders with no approval decision anywhere in migration 089; both migrations' own not-applied disclosure; existing Practice-facing modules confirmed absent from this changeset.

**Verification performed this session:** full suite 976/976 pass (954 baseline + 22 new, zero regressions). `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. ESLint on the new test file: 0 errors. Copy Quality Guard PASS (0 violations, 255 files). Production build succeeds. ### Decision 142 — Mock Programme Increment 004, Batch 001, Independent Review Execution: production reconciliation confirmed migrations 088/089 correctly applied; a real review-surface defect found and fixed — the 7 new families were loadable but neither clearly labelled nor correctly recordable as `mock_maths_independent_review` (would have silently defaulted to `content_review`, exactly the class of risk Decision 118 already named once) — corrected with a dedicated "Mock Mathematics Batch 001 Review" section, a distinct submit function, and 2 generalised (backward-compatible) shared helpers; no self-approval performed; genuine independent review not yet begun

**A. **A second, more consequential defect, found by continuing to trace the write path, not stopping at read-reachability:** `submitReview()` (`lib/adminReview.ts`) never sets `review_type` in its own `.insert()` call — it relies entirely on the table's own `'content_review'` column default (migration 059). This is not a cosmetic labelling gap; a genuine review performed through the wrong path would have been effectively lost to this batch's own governance trail.

**Part 6 — correction made, smallest bounded scope, existing architecture reused throughout, nothing redesigned:**
1. `deriveBatchReviewStatus()`/`fetchBatchReviewStatus()` (`lib/adminReview.ts`) generalised with an optional `reviewType: ReviewType = "content_review"` parameter — every existing caller (SEVEN_X/MR04_DEPTH/INC006_DEPTH) omits it and is completely unaffected, confirmed by the unchanged 987-test baseline passing with zero modification to any existing test.

**PART 2 — THE REAL CSSE PAPER BLUEPRINT**

Confidence tiers used throughout, per the directive: **A** = directly evidenced (primary CSSE source, ≥2/3 years or an explicit current-paper statement); **B** = strongly inferred (derived from A-tier facts via a stated, disclosed logical step, not itself independently observed); **C** = unknown/not sufficiently evidenced (named as a gap, not guessed).

**MATHEMATICS**
| Fact | Value | Tier | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duration | 60 minutes | A | CSSE-006/011/016 identical "60 minutes" wording, 3/3 years |
| Total marks | 60 marks | A | Identical "Total 60 marks" wording, 3/3 years |
| Question count | 20 (2023) or 21 (2021/2022) — **not stable year to year** | A (for the range), explicit known limitation for a single fixed number | Each paper's own "END OF TEST... completed N questions" line |
| Calculator/marking policy | No calculator; exact-match, no partial/method credit | A | Identical wording, 3/3 years; QT-MR-14 catalogued as this exact cross-cutting condition |
| Marks-per-question pattern | Not uniform — several numbered questions are compound (combine 2+ Question Types in sub-parts) | A for compounding as a structural fact; C for a precise, general marks-per-sub-part rule | CSSE-006 Q14 (QT-MR-03+QT-MR-07), CSSE-006 Q9 (QT-MR-10+QT-MR-01), directly cited in the Framework §6 |
| Question Type distribution | 13 substantive types (QT-MR-01–13) + 1 cross-cutting scoring condition (QT-MR-14), each independently evidenced/EMC-rated | A for the catalogue's existence and per-type evidence; confidence varies per type (HIGH for most, MEDIUM/LOW for QT-MR-02/11's search sub-format, EMC-1/2) | Framework §3, full traceability matrix §7 |
| Real difficulty distribution (as CSSE itself grades it) | **Not published anywhere in this evidence base** | **C** | No mark scheme or paper states a per-question difficulty tier; "easy/medium/hard/challenge" is Angel's own internal taxonomy, not a CSSE-evidenced category |
| Short vs multi-step balance | Compound, multi-domain questions are a confirmed, recurring structural feature (Observation 11, upgraded to HIGH confidence across all 3 years under CAP-1.1) | A | Framework §6, Observation 11 |
| Breadth of skills | Spans arithmetic, algebraic/symbolic, geometric/spatial, word-problem, number-theory domains within a single paper, consistently | A | Observation 11 |

**ENGLISH**
| Fact | Value | Tier | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper structure (current) | Comprehension + Continuous Writing only — **no Applied Reasoning** | A | Decision 58, Founder-confirmed (Part 1.3) |
| Historical structure (2021–2023 evidence base) | Comprehension (30+10 reading) + Applied Reasoning (10) + Continuous Writing (20) = 70 min total | A | CSSE-001/003/008/013 cover-page timing, cross-corroborated |
| Current total duration | **Not independently confirmed by any post-2024 primary source held in this repository** — inferred by subtracting Applied Reasoning's known 10-minute block from the historical 70-minute total (≈60 min instructional + reading time) | **B**, named explicitly as a gap | No current-year (2025/2026 entry) official English paper is held in this evidence base |
| Comprehension passage count | 1 substantial licensed literary extract per sitting | A | Migration 043's own Level A, csse.org.uk, Founder-Accepted sourcing |
| Comprehension questions attached | 11–16, attached to the one passage | A | Same source |
| Passage genre | Narrative fiction, 3/3 years observed; no non-fiction/poetry found | A (for the 3 observed instances — a small sample, disclosed) | Observation 6 |
| Comprehension mark-scheme flexibility | Markers explicitly instructed to accept paraphrased/reworded answers | A | Observation 7 |
| Continuous Writing task structure | 2 tasks — one reflective/discursive, one picture-stimulus narrative — stable, 3/3 years | A | Framework §4 (Continuous Writing) |
| Continuous Writing marks | 15 (2021, 2022) or 20 (2023, with an emerging Content 15/SPAG 5 split) | A for the raw figures; B/C for whether the 20-mark/split format is now the current standard (1 data point only) | Observations 9, 13 |
| Comprehension+AR combined marks (historical) | 45 (2021) / 40 (2023) — **total English marks (Comp+AR+Writing) stable at 60 both years** | A (a genuine, previously-unstated-this-precisely finding of this reconciliation) | Observation 4 arithmetic cross-checked against Observation 9 |
| Current Comprehension-alone marks (post-AR-removal) | **Not independently confirmed** — if the stable-60-total pattern holds, ≈40 marks | **C**, named as a gap | No current-year paper held; inferred only |
| Vocabulary/language-in-context as a distinct CSSE format | Not catalogued as its own recurring Question Type separate from the QT-RC-01–10 Comprehension set | C | Framework §3 lists no separate vocabulary format; Angel's own `english.vocabulary-in-context` is an internal Practice competency, not a CSSE-evidenced paper component |

**No manufactured precision:** "60 marks = 60 questions" is explicitly not assumed anywhere above — Mathematics resolves to 20–21 *questions* (many compound) for 60 *marks*, and English resolves to a passage-plus-tasks structure, not a flat question-per-mark count.

**PART 3 — DEFINITION OF ONE ANGEL MOCK**

**ANGEL MATHEMATICS MOCK:**
- **21 questions per form** (majority-evidenced count, 2 of 3 years; 20 is equally evidenced for the most recent year and remains an acceptable tolerance, not a violation, if a specific form's balance genuinely requires it) — **60 marks**, **60 minutes**, no calculator, exact-match marking (no partial/method credit).
- Question Type coverage: represent as many of the 13 substantive Question Types (QT-MR-01–13) as a 21-item form can genuinely support; **no single Question Type may exceed ≈15–18% of a form** (≈3–4 of 21) — a direct, deliberate correction of the live 34/194 (≈18%) QT-MR-01 concentration Decision 138/141 already found and flagged.
- Difficulty balance: since CSSE's own real difficulty distribution is not published (Part 2, C-tier), Angel's internal easy/medium/hard/challenge tiers are a **design choice, not a CSSE-evidenced requirement** — recommended working target per form: ≈15–20% easy / ≈50–55% medium / ≈25–30% hard / minimal-to-none challenge, revisable once real attempt-level difficulty data exists. Stated as a recommendation, not a frozen rule.
- Structural balance: authentic CSSE forms regularly compound two Question Types within one numbered question (Part 2). **Batch 001 and Batch 002's own 38 items are each single-Question-Type items** — a genuine, disclosed authenticity gap between the evidenced real paper structure and Angel's Mock content built so far, not previously stated this explicitly. A future batch should introduce genuine compound items; not attempted or required by this decision.

**ANGEL ENGLISH MOCK:**
- **1 passage** (licensed or Angel-original, narrative, matching the evidenced genre pattern) with **11–16 attached comprehension questions** — recommend **13–14** as a working target, near the evidenced range's midpoint.
- **2 Continuous Writing tasks** — 1 reflective/discursive, 1 picture-stimulus narrative.
- **60 marks total**; provisional split **≈40 Comprehension / 20 Writing (Content 15/SPAG 5)**, matching the most recent evidenced year and the stable-60-total finding (Part 2) — flagged B/C, not independently confirmed for the current, AR-removed paper.
- **Duration:** current total not independently confirmed (Part 2); working target **≈60 minutes instructional time (≈30 Comprehension + ≈20 Writing) + separate reading time**, inferred, not evidenced — a real gap a future increment should close with a current official source before this becomes load-bearing for a real timer.
- No Applied Reasoning content of any kind (Decision 58, reaffirmed).

Angel must not invent artificial formats to create variation — every element above is drawn from an evidenced, recurring CSSE structure, not manufactured for its own sake.

**PART 5 — ANTI-MEMORISATION MODEL**

**Five distinguished tiers, per the directive:**

1. **Exact question repetition** — the identical item, same wording, same numbers. **Never permitted within the item-level cooldown window** (recommended: **≥8 cycles / ~16 weeks** for the same learner — chosen deliberately longer than Decision 138's own "3–4 cycle" launch-floor precedent, to give real operating margin once a programme is running continuously, not just at launch).
2. **Textual near-duplication** — a reworded but recognisably-the-same item. **Treated identically to exact repetition for exposure purposes** — this is a content-review responsibility (the exact check Batch 001/002's own tests already perform against each other and against live Practice content, Decisions 141/145), not something an exposure-tracking query alone can catch, since it depends on reading meaning, not IDs.
3. **Superficial parameter variation** (same template, different numbers) — permitted as a genuinely distinct exposure **only** when hand-verified per migration 030's own precedent (difficulty, misconception target, and reasoning demand preserved, not just numbers changed) — but tracked at the **family/template level**, with its own, longer cooldown (recommended **≥16 cycles / ~32 weeks** — double the item-level window), because recognising "the same trick with new numbers" too often is itself a memorisation risk even without literal repetition.
4. **Effectively identical reasoning experience** — a different Question Type or surface format that tests the same underlying demand in a near-identical structure. Governed by the **same family/structure-level cooldown as Tier 3** — this is precisely why Batch 001/002's own "genuine reasoning-structure count, honestly reported, not conflated with row count" discipline (9 structures/18 rows; 10 structures/20 rows, Decisions 141/145) is the correct unit for exposure tracking, not the raw row.
5. **Authentic structural recurrence** — a Question Type or general format recurring because it is a genuine, stable feature of every real CSSE paper (e.g. an arithmetic question will appear in every real sitting). **Permitted, unlimited, at the Question-Type category level.** What must never recur is the *specific item, family, or reasoning structure* — not the category itself. Angel must not invent artificial question formats merely to avoid this kind of recurrence (directive's own instruction, Part 3, reaffirmed here for exposure design specifically).

**Concrete controls, evidence-graded:**

| Control | State | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Learner question-exposure history | **Reconstructable today, zero new schema** (`ali_mock_attempt.assigned_question_ids`/`form_id`) | Reuse unchanged (Decision 138 Part 4A) |
| Passage-exposure history | **Real for Practice, unwired for Mock** (`passageGroupingKeyOf`) | Extend the same keying convention once `ali_passage_bank` is populated (Decision 138 Part 4B) |
| Family/structure-exposure history | **No query exists anywhere** | **New finding of this decision** — a bounded, additive query over existing `family_id`-tagged data, no new table required |
| Form-exposure history | **Reconstructable today** (`ali_mock_attempt.form_id`) | Reuse; no new schema needed for the *history*, only for the *policy* below |
| Cooldown periods | Item ≥8 cycles; family/structure ≥16 cycles; **passage: recommend no repeat within one continuous learner enrolment at all** (per the directive's own explicit "particularly high memorisation risk" instruction) | New recommendation, Founder confirmation needed before this becomes a hard rule |
| Max repeated-item % per paper | **0% within the item-cooldown window** (hard rule); **≤15% (≈3 of 21) once outside it** | New recommendation |
| Max repeated-reasoning-structure % | **≤25% of a form's structures may repeat one seen in the prior 4 cycles** — tighter than the item-level bound, because structure-recognition is faster to memorise than literal recall | New recommendation |
| Passage reuse | Effectively never per learner within one programme enrolment (see cooldown row above) | New recommendation |
| Form retirement | `ali_mock_form.active` exists; no policy layer above it | Still unbuilt (Decision 139 Part 9, unchanged) |
| Question retirement | `ali_question_bank.active`/`content_version` support versioned retirement | Reuse unchanged (Decision 138 Part 4F) |
| Reserve capacity | See Part 9 | New |
| Previously-exposed content | Fully queryable via the mechanisms above | Query needs to be *built*, not the underlying data |

Everything already reconstructable is reused unchanged, matching this project's own repeated pattern (Decisions 133/135/138 each found existing capability rather than inventing a parallel one). The one genuinely new schema/code gap this decision surfaces precisely — not previously named this specifically — is the **family/structure-level exposure query** (row 3 above); everything else is either already reusable data or a policy/threshold decision layered on top of it.

**PART 6 — MOCK FORM BANK MODEL**

Confirms and extends Decision 138 Part 7/11's own B/A-hybrid recommendation, reaffirmed: **reviewed, frozen forms, algorithmically candidate-composed then independently human-reviewed** — never fully dynamic per-attempt assembly, which would be structurally incompatible with `ali_mock_form.question_manifest`'s existing frozen-snapshot reproducibility guarantee (Decision 138 Part 4G, unchanged) and with independent pre-review (a form that does not exist until attempt-time cannot be reviewed before a learner sits it).

```
Reviewed Content Pool (independently_validated + mock_eligible, once the pool-gate exists)
  → Pool-level Mock-Eligible Gate (still unbuilt, Decision 138)
    → Algorithmic Candidate Composition (reuses selectQuestions()'s weighted-pool/balance machinery, Decision 138 Part 7)
      → Independent Human Review (extends ali_family_review, Decision 139)
        → Frozen ali_mock_form row (subject-pure, question_manifest sealed)
          → FORM BANK (multiple pre-assembled, reviewed, frozen forms held in reserve — not one form generated on demand)
            → Form-Routing-by-Exposure (NEW, this decision's own contribution — Part 6a below)
              → Learner's Sealed Attempt (ali_mock_attempt, migrations 069-071/085/086)
```

**Part 6a — the one refinement this decision adds to the pipeline Decision 138/139 already designed:** neither prior decision specified *how* a specific learner, at cycle-start, is routed to a specific already-frozen form from the bank. This decision names that step explicitly: a **form-routing function**, evaluated at `mock_create_cycle_attempt()` time, selecting from the active, reviewed form bank the form whose complete `question_manifest` has the *least* recent-or-cooling-down overlap with that learner's own exposure history (Part 5), never first-available or random selection. This is a query over the exposure-history mechanism, not a new content-delivery path — reproducibility, review, sealing, and audit all remain exactly as already proven. Not built by this decision.

A learner must not receive the same complete form twice — this is structurally guaranteed once form-exposure history (already reconstructable, Part 5) is consulted by the routing step, with no new table required for that guarantee specifically.

|---|---|---|
| First-Mock activation floor | ≥21–25 `mock_eligible` items, spanning enough distinct families/Question Types to assemble one authentic, no-single-QT-dominant form | Part 3's own form definition; Batch 001+002 combined (38, 10 of 13 QTs, QT-MR-01/08/12 still absent) is sufficient in *count* but not yet in *breadth* — a small, **targeted** gap-filling batch (capped, authentic QT-MR-01 representation + remaining QTs) is the right next content step, not raw-volume Batch 003 |
| Controlled-launch floor (3–4 non-repeating cycles) | **≈80–85** | **Reaffirmed unchanged from Decision 138/140** — correct as a launch floor, explicitly not sufficient beyond it (Part 1.4) |
| 26-week (13-cycle) sustainable | **A rolling floor of ≈150–170, maintained continuously** (≈8 cycles' worth at 21/form, matching the Part 5 item-cooldown window), replenished by ongoing batch authoring as content ages into reusability — **not** a one-off 273-item target |
| 52-week (26-cycle) sustainable | **The same ≈150–170 rolling floor**, PLUS a **family/structural-diversity floor of ≥40–50 distinct families/structures** (not raw item count alone) — this is the real long-run lever, matching Decision 138 Part 5's own "majority-parameterised strategy" finding, reaffirmed: depth of genuine structural variety, not a bigger raw number, is what keeps the 16-week/32-week structural cooldown (Part 5) meaningful at sustained scale |

This explicitly does **not** ask for 546 (the 52-week naive ceiling) or even 273 (the 26-week naive ceiling) — the tiered reuse model in Part 5 is what makes ≈150–170, continuously maintained, a defensible standing floor instead.

**PART 2 — AUTHENTIC MATHEMATICS PAPER MODEL: GROUPED-QUESTION ARCHITECTURE**

**Direct schema finding, confirmed by reading the live migrations, not assumed:** `ali_question_bank` (migration 005) has exactly one `prompt jsonb` column per row; for Mathematics, `prompt` conforms to `MathsQuestion` (`types/index.ts`): one `question` string, one scalar `answer` (`number | string`), an optional flat `workingSteps: string[]`, and exactly one `marks: number`. No column, JSONB key, or related table anywhere in the schema (confirmed by a full search of every `ALTER TABLE ali_question_bank` across migrations 007/009/030/035/084) represents a numbered-question-group identifier, an ordered subpart list, or a per-subpart mark. `mock_score_attempt()` (migration 074) confirms this is load-bearing, not incidental: its scoring loop reads `(v_bank_row.prompt->>'marks')::numeric` once per `question_id`, scores each `question_id` as one atomic pass/fail/partial unit, and sums directly into `v_raw_achieved`/`v_raw_available` — there is no group-rollup step anywhere in the scored output (`question_outcomes` is a flat array keyed by `questionId`). `ali_mock_form.question_manifest` (migration 070) is a flat JSONB array of `{question_id, ...}` entries with no ordering, grouping, or shared-context key. **Batch 001 and Batch 002's own 38 authored rows (Decisions 141/145) are each exactly this atomic shape** — one prompt, one scalar answer, one marks value — confirming the gap is real in already-authored content, not merely theoretical.

**Classification: B — bounded extension required, not an architectural conflict.** Nothing proven needs to be undone: scoring, redaction (migrations 069/071), sealed-content RLS, and `question_manifest`'s frozen-snapshot reproducibility guarantee (Decision 138 Part 4G) all operate correctly today at the granularity of one gradable "response component" per row — a genuine CSSE subpart with its own scalar answer and its own marks is already exactly representable as one `ali_question_bank` row. What is missing is the layer *above* that: a way to say "these N rows are subparts (a), (b), (c)... of numbered question group 7, sharing context/diagram X, worth Y marks combined." This is additive because:
1. A **grouping key** (e.g. `question_group_id text`, `group_order smallint`, `subpart_label text`, an optional `shared_context_ref text`) can be added to `ali_question_bank` as nullable columns — every existing row (including all 38 Batch 001/002 items) remains valid, unchanged, as an implicit "group of one" (`question_group_id = id`, no rewrite required).
2. `question_manifest`'s JSONB array entries can carry the same grouping keys additively — existing readers of the flat `question_id` list are unaffected; no breaking change to `mock_get_question()`, `mock_start_attempt()`, or any existing test.
3. `mock_score_attempt()`'s existing per-`question_id` loop (migration 074) can be extended with a **secondary group-level rollup** computed from the same already-collected `v_outcomes` — summing already-scored subpart marks into a group total for reporting purposes — additive to the loop, not a rewrite of its per-item scoring logic.
4. Marks-per-subpart remains a **content-authoring-time judgement call, not a schema question** — Part 2's own finding in Decision 146 (marks-per-question pattern not uniform, C-tier — no general rule evidenced) is reaffirmed unchanged; the schema extension makes representing an authored subpart mark possible, it does not itself supply the number.

**Not implemented by this decision.** The exact grouping mechanism (additive columns on `ali_question_bank` versus a small new `ali_mock_question_group` lookup table) is left as an open, bounded design choice for the increment that actually builds this — both are viable and neither requires undoing anything proven; the choice depends on whether group-level metadata (e.g. a group's own shared diagram/context asset) grows large enough to warrant its own row, a decision better made against real authored content than in the abstract here.

**PART 3 — MOCK QUALITY PRINCIPLE, RECORDED**

The seven governing objectives (authentic experience, educational usefulness, sufficient remediation time, anti-memorisation, sustainable capacity, longitudinal comparison, learner wellbeing) are recorded as the standing evaluation frame for every future Mock architecture decision, superseding no prior decision — Decision 138/146's own capacity work already implicitly optimised for several of these (sufficient remediation time via cooldown windows, anti-memorisation via the five-tier model); this decision makes the frame explicit so a future increment does not silently default to frequency-maximisation. **Mock frequency is not a target.** This principle governs Parts 4–5 below directly.

---

**PART 4 — ADAPTIVE MOCK CADENCE**

**A. First Mock — not a calendar entitlement.** No fixed elapsed-time threshold unlocks the first Full Mock. A genuine, already-live mechanism exists and is the correct foundation for this: `lib/learningEngine/mockReadiness.ts`'s `assessMockReadiness()` — a pure categorical dispatch over three already-real, already-computed Educational Intelligence signals (`hasAnyEvidence` from `LearnerIntelligenceProfile`, `mockAttemptCount`, `topTriggerReason` from the real Recommendation Engine's own ranking) — returning one of three verdicts: `"practice-first"`, `"first-mock-valuable"`, `"mock-valuable"`. Confirmed live at two real call sites (`app/mocks/page.tsx`'s Mock Centre card, `components/parent/CssePathwayParentContent.tsx`'s Parent Dashboard), computing a genuine `"Ready for your first Mock"`-equivalent state (`"first-mock-valuable"`, fired when `hasAnyEvidence` is true and `mockAttemptCount === 0`) and a `"Nearly ready"`-equivalent state (`"practice-first"` with `hasAnyEvidence = true`, distinguished from the no-evidence-at-all case via the separate `hasAnyEvidence` field `CssePathwayParentContent.tsx` already carries alongside the verdict). **This is not a new concept to invent — it already exists, live, and already expresses close to what the Founder's Part 4A describes.** **Two disclosed gaps, found by tracing further, not stopping at "a readiness signal exists":** (1) it is currently **informational-only** — a status card and explanation, never consulted by `mock_create_attempt`/`mock_start_new_cycle` at the database layer, so it does not actually gate anything today; (2) `mockAttemptCount` is sourced from `getMockResults()` (`lib/mockProgress.ts`), confirmed by Decision 59 to be the legacy, localStorage-based mock-history mechanism, **not** the real, persisted `ali_mock_attempt`/`ali_mock_cycle` tables — meaning today's readiness signal counts a different, older notion of "mock attempt" than the one the governed cycle architecture (migration 085) actually persists. Both are named as bounded, EXTEND-classified gaps (Part 11), not reasons to distrust the underlying dispatch design, which is sound and reusable.

**B. Normal cadence after first Mock — approximately 28 days / four weeks.** Reaffirms the intended educational cycle stated by the directive (Mock → Diagnose → Recommend → Reteach/Practise → Retrieve → Demonstrate Improvement → Next Mock) and confirms its middle stages already have real, live infrastructure to draw on: `getRecommendations()` (the Recommendation Engine already read by `mockReadiness.ts` itself) and the Revision Planner (`/learning-intelligence/parent/revision-planner`, already linked from `assessMockReadiness()`'s own `"practice-first"` verdict) already perform genuine diagnose→recommend work today, entirely independent of Mock cadence. **A disclosed non-conflation, restated for this decision specifically because the new model risks re-introducing it:** `RETRIEVAL_INTERVAL_DAYS.maintenanceWindow = 14` (`lib/ali/exposureIntelligence.ts`, confirmed still present, unchanged) is a genuine, unrelated, Practice-only spaced-retrieval constant — Decision 138 already flagged this exact 14-day coincidence once; it must not be read as connected to, or a precedent for, the Mock cycle's own interval, even though this decision's own Part 4C now uses "approximately 14 days" for the accelerated Mock case specifically. Two independently-arrived-at 14s, still unrelated, still not to be merged — reaffirmed, not re-derived.

**C. Accelerated cadence — retained, role changed.** The existing ~14-day mechanism (migration 085) is preserved as a real, reusable piece of plumbing, but its meaning changes from *the* interval to *an* interval available only when Educational-Intelligence evidence justifies shortening the ~28-day normal gap. The directive's own named examples (remediation completed, evidence materially changed, weaknesses addressed, timing/technique rather than substantive gaps, exam proximity, sufficient fresh protected content) are recorded as the qualitative shape of this future decision, **deliberately not hard-coded as boolean rules here**, per explicit instruction — the Educational Intelligence Engine must own the actual decision logic, drawing on the same class of signal `mockReadiness.ts` already demonstrates is available (real recommendation/evidence data), not a new parallel signal source.

**PART 5 — PREPARATION PHASE MODEL**

Four conceptual phases recorded, per the directive, as architecture only:

| Phase | Cadence | Emphasis |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Foundation | No automatic Mock cadence | Build competency coverage/evidence before any first Mock |
| 2 — Development | ~28-day normal Full Mock cadence | Diagnosis, remediation, teaching, practice, durable improvement between Mocks |
| 3 — Exam Readiness | May shorten toward ~14 days when evidence/proximity/capacity justify it | Increasing realistic-assessment frequency, evidence-gated |
| 4 — Final Preparation | Strategic, not maximised | Realistic Mock use without unnecessary repeated testing merely because calendar capacity exists |

**Per the directive's own explicit instruction, no new learner-state machine is proposed.** Reconciliation found `mockReadiness.ts`'s three-verdict categorical dispatch is a **partial, reusable foundation specifically for the Phase 1→Phase 2 transition** (its `"practice-first"`/`"first-mock-valuable"` verdicts already distinguish "not ready" from "ready for a first Mock," the exact Phase 1/2 boundary) — but it does not, today, represent Phase 3/4's evidence-gated acceleration or de-escalation, and does not persist a phase as durable state anywhere (it is recomputed fresh on every page load from live signals, not stored). **Whether that recompute-on-read pattern is sufficient to represent all four phases, or whether Phase 3/4 genuinely need a persisted phase marker, is named here as an open design question for the increment that builds this — not resolved by this decision, per the directive's own instruction not to build a new state machine speculatively.**

**PART 7 — ANTI-MEMORISATION IMPLICATIONS**

Decision 146's five-tier model (exact repetition / textual near-duplication / superficial parameter variation / effectively-identical-reasoning-experience / authentic structural recurrence) is **preserved unchanged** — reaffirmed, not re-derived. This decision adds one refinement the authentic-paper hierarchy (Part 2) makes newly relevant: **Tier 3 ("superficial parameter variation") must now be assessed at the response-component level, not only the whole-item level**, once grouped questions exist — changing only the numbers in one subpart of a multi-part group while leaving its sibling subparts, shared context, and overall reasoning chain untouched is the same Tier-3 risk Decision 146 already named for a standalone item, applying identically inside a group. The directive's own worked example (repeatedly re-numbering "Find 15% of X" is not sufficient diversity; genuine diversity comes from direct calculation / discount / increase-decrease / reverse-percentage / comparison / money-context / multistep-context / linked-question-group reasoning as **distinct Tier 4/5 structures**, not Tier 3 restyling) is recorded as the concrete standard future Mathematics batches must be authored and reviewed against — consistent with, and a direct application of, Decision 141/145's own "genuine reasoning-structure count, not row count" discipline, now extended explicitly to cover linked-group reasoning as one of the legitimate structural forms. No artificial structure unsupported by CSSE evidence is invented here or endorsed for future authoring, per the directive's own instruction.

**PART 8 — CAPACITY MODEL CORRECTION**

**Decision 146's ≈150–170 (26/52-week) rolling-floor figure is superseded as a unit of measurement, not merely re-scaled to a new magnitude, per explicit instruction not to simply pick another row-count number.** Two independent reasons compound: (1) Part 2 above establishes that a raw `ali_question_bank` row is not a stable proxy for one authentic assessment experience — a numbered question group may contain several rows (subparts), so a fixed row-count target implicitly assumes a group-size ratio that has never been evidenced or decided; (2) Decision 146's own demand table (Part 4 of that decision) was built on a uniform 14-day-cycle assumption across the full 12–52-week window, which Part 4 of this decision replaces with a cadence that varies by phase — the cycle counts that raw figure was derived from no longer hold as a single constant either.

**What today's schema and code can already measure, confirmed by direct reading, reused not rebuilt:** raw `ali_question_bank` row counts by subject/status/skill (live queries, unchanged); `family_id`-grouped counts (Decisions 138/141/145's own "genuine reasoning-structure count" discipline, proven, reusable); per-item exposure history (`ali_mock_attempt.assigned_question_ids`, Part 1.1); difficulty-tier distribution (`content_difficulty`, live). **What does not exist and would be required for a genuine educational-unit capacity model**, named as gaps, not built: a numbered-question-group count distinct from row count (blocked on Part 2's own schema extension); a per-form subpart/response-component density measure; a family/structure-diversity measure independent of raw row count (the *building block* — `family_id` grouping — exists, but no query currently expresses "how many genuinely distinct Full-Mock-worth of structural variety does the current pool support"); a linked-versus-independent-reasoning ratio per form (depends on Part 2); a visual/data/context-diversity measure (no schema field distinguishes a question's context/diagram/data-table type from its Question Type today).

**Recommended future capacity model, expressed in educational units, no number supplied:** the target output of a future capacity-measurement increment should be **"N genuinely fresh, authentic Full Mock experiences this pool can safely support for one learner before Part 5/7's cooldown thresholds are exhausted,"** computed from: (a) reviewed numbered-question-groups (not rows) meeting Part 2's structural definition; (b) their aggregate subpart/response-component count against the Part 3 (Decision 146) target marks/question-count envelope; (c) family/reasoning-structure diversity (already-buildable from `family_id`) weighted against the Part 7 cooldown windows; (d) Question-Type and difficulty balance (already measurable); (e) linked-group-reasoning representation, once Part 2 exists. **This decision does not compute this figure** — doing so requires Part 2's schema extension to exist first (a group cannot be counted before it can be represented), so the measurement model itself is named here as the next content-adjacent architecture step, not performed now.

**PART 9 — ENGLISH CONSEQUENCE**

The same principle applies with **greater force**, reaffirming and not contradicting Decision 146 Part 8's near-permanent passage-cooldown recommendation (no genuine contradiction found by this reconciliation). A single `ali_passage_bank`/Comprehension row count was already, even before this decision, an unreliable proxy — Decision 138 itself already found "a passage with fewer than 11–16 real attached questions does not count as a Mock-ready passage regardless of its row count," the exact row-count-versus-educational-unit distinction this decision now generalises to Mathematics. The genuinely fresh unit for English is **the complete (passage + its full attached question set + its own Writing-prompt pairing for that sitting)**, not any one of those three counted alone — a passage reused with an entirely new question set is not a fresh Mock experience by this decision's own Part 7 standard (Tier 3/4 risk at the passage level, arguably the single highest-stakes case named anywhere in this model, per the directive's own "particularly high memorisation risk" instruction, Decision 146). No English content is authored, and the passage-cooldown recommendation is not altered, by this decision.

**PART 7 — FINAL CROSS-SUBJECT ASSESSMENT HIERARCHY**

The conceptual hierarchy (PAPER → SECTION → SOURCE/STIMULUS → NUMBERED QUESTION → SUBPART → RESPONSE COMPONENT → MARK) is adopted as the standing conceptual frame, with the directive's own explicit caveat preserved: not every subject uses every level, and simpler structures omit levels naturally. This decision's own implementation represents exactly two of these levels concretely in schema — NUMBERED QUESTION (via a shared `question_group_id`) and SUBPART/RESPONSE COMPONENT (via `group_order` + free-text `subpart_label`, deliberately collapsed into one flexible field rather than a rigid third schema level, Part 8 below) — because those are the only levels any currently-authored or evidence-catalogued content actually needs represented today. SECTION and PAPER-level composition remain conceptual only (no `assessment_section` table, no manifest population) since no form exists to compose. SOURCE/STIMULUS remains served by the existing, unmodified `ali_passage_bank` for English and by a within-item scenario for Mathematics (Part 8 below) — no new stimulus-content table was required or built.

**PART 8 — SCHEMA CHANGES**

Migration 093 (`supabase/migrations/093_mock_assessment_hierarchy_foundation.sql`, **NOT APPLIED**) adds exactly 4 nullable columns to `ali_question_bank`, plus one partial index and four column comments — no other table touched:

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `question_group_id` | `text`, nullable | NULL (every existing row, unchanged) = standalone atomic item. Shared non-NULL value = subparts/response-components of one numbered question. |
| `group_order` | `smallint`, nullable, `>= 1` when present | Deterministic 1-based position within a group. |
| `subpart_label` | `text`, nullable | Free-text display label (e.g. `"(a)"`, `"6(b)-i"`) — deliberately not a constrained enum or a second grouping level. |
| `marking_mode` | `text`, nullable, one of `deterministic`/`structured_acceptable_response`/`criterion_rubric` | Classification only, no scoring behaviour. NULL is a deliberate non-claim (not defaulted to `deterministic`) — no per-row classification is asserted for any of the 331+ pre-existing rows, since none was actually verified this session. |

**Deliberate, evidenced design decision — a new column, not a repurposed one:** `family_id` (sibling reasoning-variant grouping, migration 030) and `learning_unit_id` (migration 007) were both inspected and rejected as the grouping key. Direct reading of `lib/ali/exposureIntelligence.ts` this session confirmed `groupingKeyOf()` — the function the live Practice selection engine actually calls (`lib/learningEngine/sessionGenerator.ts`) — reads `q.familyId ?? q.learningUnitId` for **every subject**, not only English. Repurposing `learning_unit_id` as a Mathematics numbered-question-group key would have risked silently feeding Mock-only grouping metadata into live Practice exposure/clustering logic for any Mathematics row lacking a `family_id` — exactly the outcome the directive's Part 11 forbids. `question_group_id` is a genuinely new column, read by no existing selection, scoring, or rendering code path today, confirmed by a dedicated structural test — zero collision risk by construction, not by convention. (`passageGroupingKeyOf()`, the other `learning_unit_id` consumer, was separately confirmed already subject-gated to `"english"` only and was never at risk — the wider, ungated `groupingKeyOf()` is what ruled out reuse.)

No `shared_context_id`/stimulus-content table was added (Part 9 below). No third schema-level grouping table. No RLS or grant change (migration 084's `ali_question_bank_select_all` policy governs row visibility, not individual columns — confirmed by direct reading). No new SQL function.

**PART 9 — SHARED-CONTEXT/STIMULUS DECISION**

Classified, per the directive's own A/B/C scheme, as **two separate findings, not one**:

1. **The grouping-relationship mechanism** — classified **A, an existing mechanism already subject-neutral by design**: the general pattern "several `ali_question_bank` rows share one parent-context identifier" already exists precisely once, correctly, for English (`learning_unit_id` → `ali_passage_bank`). Migration 093's `question_group_id` extends the same *pattern* (a shared identifier linking several rows to one parent numbered question) to a genuinely new, safe column rather than the same literal one (Part 8's own reasoning for why the *literal column* could not safely be shared).
2. **The context/stimulus content-storage mechanism** (`ali_passage_bank` itself) — classified **C, separate mechanisms remain safer**: its columns (`title`, `original_text`, `text_type`, `genre`, `word_count`, `reading_complexity`, `copyright_status`) are literary-extract-specific and would misrepresent a Mathematics shared scenario/diagram/data-table if reused directly — the directive's own explicit "do not misuse English passage architecture merely because it exists" instruction, applied. **No new Mathematics context-content table was built** — no currently-authored or evidence-catalogued Mathematics content (checked directly, Part 12 below) requires one yet; a shared Maths scenario can, for now, be represented the same way passage text was represented before `ali_passage_bank` existed (duplicated within each subpart's own `prompt`), exactly mirroring migration 043's own disclosed evolutionary precedent (built only once real, multi-question sharing became a genuine integrity risk). Named as a future **B — bounded, subject-neutral or Maths-specific context mechanism** item (Part 18), not built speculatively now.

**PART 5 — A CRITICAL, VERIFIED, PRE-EXISTING FINDING: PRACTICE IS NOT ACTUALLY GATED AGAINST MOCK-CANDIDATE CONTENT**

**This finding predates this session's own work and is not introduced by either track's content.** It is disclosed here, prominently, because this increment materially increases its blast radius (26 more rows now exposed to it) and because every decision in this arc back to Decision 141 has described Mock candidate content as "quarantined from Practice," a description this finding shows is not actually true at the code level, whatever the eligibility-status *count* evidence has correctly, but only partially, shown.

**Verified directly by reading the real, live source (not inferred, not assumed):**
- `lib/ali/questionBank.ts`'s `PRACTICE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES` constant (line 51) includes `"authentic_assessment_candidate"` and `"independently_validated"`, not only `"practice_eligible"`. Its own `fetchQuestionBank()` function filters solely on `active`, `provenance !== "evidence_only"`, and membership in this set — nothing else.
- `lib/learningEngine/sessionGenerator.ts`, the REAL learner-facing Practice session generator (`generatePersonalisedSession`, called by the live Practice pathway), calls `fetchQuestionBank(supabase, area.subject, "csse")` directly (line 277), filters only to QT-tagged rows (line 278), and the resulting `candidatePool` (line 358) is passed straight into `selectQuestions()` (`lib/ali/selection.ts`, confirmed by direct search to contain **zero** references to `eligibilityStatus`/`eligibility_status` anywhere) — whose output becomes the actual `activities` array returned to, and rendered for, the real learner. No `lib/learningEngine/*` file references `eligibility_status` at all (confirmed by a repository-wide search returning zero files).
- Migrations 095/097/098 (this increment) use `subject = 'maths'`/`'english'`, `pathway = array['csse']`, `skill = 'QT-*'` — exactly the fields `fetchQuestionBank`/`sessionGenerator` select on. So do migrations 088/090/091/093/094 (Batch 001/002, already applied, already `independently_validated` in production).

**What this means concretely:** the 38 Mathematics Mock candidate questions already `independently_validated` in live production (Batch 001 + Batch 002) are, right now, structurally eligible to be selected and served inside an ordinary learner's real Practice session — not merely sitting inert as "Mock candidates," contrary to how Decisions 141/144/145/149/150 have each described Practice as unaffected. The Founder's own repeated production evidence that Mathematics `practice_eligible` **count** remains 194 is correct and was never in question — that count only ever measured rows whose `eligibility_status` literally equals `'practice_eligible'`, a narrower and different claim from "no Mock candidate row is ever served to a Practice learner." Those are two different claims, and only the first has actually been verified against production; the second is contradicted by this session's own direct reading of the serving code path.

**Not fixed by this session, deliberately:** this is Practice-selection code (`lib/ali/questionBank.ts`, `lib/learningEngine/sessionGenerator.ts`), explicitly forbidden to this increment by the directive's own Part 8 and Absolute Boundaries ("Do not modify: Practice selection; Practice eligibility"). Any fix here (most plausibly, narrowing `PRACTICE_ELIGIBLE_STATUSES` to just `{practice_eligible, mock_eligible}`, or excluding rows with a Mock-programme provenance marker) is itself a Practice-behaviour change requiring its own scoped, Founder-authorised decision with its own regression verification against 8+ increments of prior assumptions — not a side effect of a content-authoring increment.

**Recommendation:** before migrations 095–099 are applied, and ideally before any further Mock content increment is authored, this gap should be closed with its own dedicated decision, since applying these migrations will not only create 26 new Mock candidates as intended, but will also, as an unintended and previously undisclosed side effect, make all 26 immediately eligible for real Practice serving before any independent review of them has taken place.
